title: 8 best link-in-bio tools for brands and creators in 2026

Between character count limitations and linking restrictions, one clickable URL in your bio could fix a lot of problems.


[Link-in-bio](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/link-in-bio/) tools let you centralize your social links with a dynamic landing page that hosts all the URLs for your social posts. That means a single link will lead to many destinations. You just need to update the landing page with the destination URL for every new post you share on your socials.


Your bio link stays the same, but people *still* get to visit the intended destination for your latest posts.


So link-in-bio tools for Instagram are especially useful for bypassing the platform’s restrictions against clickable links in the caption. This leads to real traffic that you could otherwise lose without a clickable URL to lead visitors to the right destination. And traffic could ultimately turn into conversions.


In this post, we rank the best link-in-bio tools to back up your social media efforts. Let’s dive in.


## 1. Sprout Social


**Best for:** Social teams that need link-in-bio features baked into a larger social media workflow


[SproutLink](https://sproutsocial.com/features/link-in-bio/) is a built-in link-in-bio tool that comes with your Sprout Social plan. It lets you build a custom landing page featuring a clickable, shoppable grid that mirrors your Instagram. So when people click on your bio link, it’s easier to pick up where they left off on the platform.


You can create a custom branded URL that adds credibility to your link, giving audiences the confidence to click through. Sprout’s analysis even found that our[link-in-bio Instagram tool](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/link-in-bio-instagram-tool/) led to a 17% average lift in profile engagement per day for customers using SproutLink.


The feature integrates with the rest of your Instagram publishing workflow, which means you get to add the destination links as you create and schedule new posts. And the clickable posts will automatically appear in your custom landing page.


This saves you the trouble of using a dedicated tool to add and manage your links separately from your publishing ecosystem.


**Key features:**


- Custom branded URL
- Visual grid-style landing page
- Hourly-updated link analytics
- Link scheduling
- Branding and customization


**Pros:**


- Seamless integration with social media management workflows
- Robust analytics insights into page views and per-post click counts


*Source:[Sprout Social](https://sproutsocial.com/features/link-in-bio/)*


## 2. Linktree


**Best for:** Solopreneurs and individual creators needing a tool with fast, no-frills setup


[Linktree](https://linktr.ee/) is a straightforward tool often touted as the “original” in the link-in-bio category. You can choose from pre-built designs to create a[landing page](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/landing-page-examples/) that hosts all your links in one place.


The tool connects your content across different social networks, not just Instagram. You can even use QR codes to send offline traffic to your Linktree page.


The free tier lets you manage an unlimited number of basic links and comes with limited analytics. Upgrading to a paid plan unlocks deeper analytics and customization tools.


**Key features:**


- Multi-platform link management
- Supports unlimited links
- QR codes for offline traffic
- Traffic monetization support
- Basic publishing and scheduling tools


**Pros:**


- Free tier available
- Easy, beginner-friendly setup


**Cons:**


- Branding and customization require paid upgrades
- Bare-bones analytics with the free plan


*Source:[Linktree](https://linktr.ee/)*


## 3. Beacons


**Best for:** Creators needing a tool to monetize their social media links


[Beacons](https://beacons.ai/i/app-pages/link-in-bio) is an all-in-one creator platform with a built-in link-in-bio tool. It functions as a creator-commerce suite rather than a simple link page. So in addition to managing your URLs, you get to build a unified business hub featuring images, music, products and signup forms.


The free plan comes with basic analytics and a customizable link in bio. Custom domains and advanced marketing features require a paid upgrade.


**Key features:**


- Built-in storefront
- Multimedia embedding
- Email capture, media kits, tipping
- Digital products and affiliate links
- Auto-updating media kits
- Basic link analytics


**Pros:**


- Free tier available
- Robust monetization features


**Cons:**


- Functions separately from your publishing workflow
- 9% seller fees with the free plan


*Source:[Beacons](https://beacons.ai/i/app-pages/link-in-bio)*


## 4. Milkshake


**Best for:** Beginners needing a fast, visual, mobile-first builder


[Milkshake](https://milkshake.app/) positions itself as a “website builder” rather than a link-in-bio tool. You can build a custom website by putting together multiple “Cards” (or pages) that each serves a specific purpose. The Links Card lets you stack multiple URLs that lead to different destinations, functioning as a link-in-bio page.


The template-driven, mobile-native design mimics a mini app rather than a scrolling link list. This makes it ideal for beginners who need to quickly put together a custom page for their links.


The free version of the tool comes with up to 30 days of analytics data and basic customization.


**Key features:**


- App-based website builder
- Supports unlimited links
- QR codes for offline traffic
- Link analytics
- Monetization tools


**Pros:**


- Free tier available
- Fast and easy to use for beginners


**Cons:**


- Functions separately from your publishing workflow
- 12% seller fees with the free plan


Source: *[Milkshake](https://milkshake.app/)*


## 5. Shorby


**Best for:** Marketers needing better tracking and campaign control


[Shorby](https://shorby.com/instagram/) is one of the best link-in-bio tools if you want access to real-time link data. The tool automatically keeps track of all the clicks coming from your personalized URL in real time.


It even integrates with tracking pixels, allowing you to retarget custom audiences with the most relevant ads. This makes it ideal for teams running paid or attribution-sensitive campaigns.


**Key features:**


- Pixel tracking and retargeting
- Built-in link shortening
- Messenger links
- Rich links


**Pros:**


- Offers real-time click insights and retargeting
- Supports extensive personalization


**Cons:**


- Functions separately from your publishing workflow
- Limited free trial period (5 days)


Source: *[Shorby](https://shorby.com/instagram/)*


## 6. Carrd


**Best for:** Brands wanting more design freedom than a template allows


Like Milkshake,[Carrd](https://carrd.com/) functions as a mini website builder rather than a simple link-in-bio tool. You can choose from dozens of pre-built templates or start your own design from scratch, giving you more control over how your page looks.


You can build up to three responsive sites with the free plan. Upgrading to a paid plan lets you remove the Carrd branding and unlocks site analytics, custom domains and forms. You even get to embed custom codes and widgets from services like Stripe and Typeform, streamlining form submissions and payments.


**Key features:**


- Pre-built and custom templates
- Responsive design
- Up to three sites free


**Pros:**


- Free tier available
- Strong layout control


**Cons:**


- Site analytics and embeds require a paid upgrade
- Free plan comes with Carrd branding
- Functions separately from your publishing workflow


Source: *[Carrd](https://carrd.com/)*


## 7. Stan Store


**Best for:** Creators selling digital products or coaching directly


[Stan Store](https://www.stan.store/) is an all-in-one tool for creators to manage all their content links, courses, bookings and analytics in one place. Instead of “one link, multiple destinations,” the tool directly hosts everything you need to sell in-bio.


So the page itself serves as a centralized storefront, where people can book a consultation or access your digital courses. It even supports one-tap checkout to reduce friction and speed up the journey from discovery to purchase, ultimately turning engagements into real[social media ROI](https://sproutsocial.com/roi/social-media-roi/) .


**Key features:**


- Built-in storefront
- Calendar invites and bookings
- Course builder
- Audience analytics
- Lead magnets and email collection
- One-tap checkout


**Pros:**


- Offers direct selling tools
- Zero transaction fees


**Cons:**


- Functions separately from your publishing workflow
- Complex and busy interface


Source: *[Stan Store](https://www.stan.store/)*


## 8. Lnk.Bio


**Best for:** For users wanting the simplest possible link list without the extra features


If a simple link list is really *all* that you’re after, then[Lnk.Bio](https://lnk.bio/) is as good as it gets. The free plan lets you add unlimited links to your page, with the option to embed multimedia and add maps.


A paid upgrade unlocks the Instagram-style grid layout with password-protected links, advanced analytics and UTM presets.


**Key features:**


- Multimedia embedding
- QR codes for offline traffic
- 577 free templates
- Supports unlimited links


**Pros:**


- Free tier available with low-cost starter plans
- Straightforward and easy to get started


**Cons:**


- Functions separately from your publishing workflow


Source: *[Lnk.Bio](https://lnk.bio/)*


## How to choose the best link-in-bio tool for your brand


Deciding on the best link-in-bio tool for your brand starts with asking the right questions:


### What do you need it for?


Start by matching your tool choice to your goal. What’s your biggest priority? This will help you focus on the tools with the exact features you need. Options like Stan Store and Beacons may work best for creators needing a tool to streamline selling. But Shorby works best for teams that need better campaign tracking.


Meanwhile, those who need a simple link hub will find tools like Lnk.Bio and Linktree more than satisfactory. But SproutLink integrates directly into your publishing workflow, making it ideal for teams that need a link-in-bio tool to support a larger[Instagram marketing strategy](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/instagram-marketing-strategy/) .


### Who’s going to use it?


Are you an individual creator or a[one-person team](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/how-to-manage-social-media-as-a-one-person-team/) ? Or perhaps you need a tool that offers multi-account access for an entire team. You can decide on the right fit based on the number of profiles you can connect with a single account and whether you can share admin access.


For example, Sprout gives you a dedicated SproutLink site for each Instagram profile connected to your account. That means if you connect all five profiles permitted with your Essentials plan, you can have five separate SproutLink pages for each connected profile.


### What’s your budget?


Cost is another major consideration, especially for smaller teams on a budget. But you still need to consider the tradeoff.


While many link-in-bio tools come with a free plan, this usually means limited[analytics](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/social-media-analytics/) insights and customization. Moreover, you need to consider how the tool fits into your overall publishing ecosystem and what other capabilities it offers.


Sure, one tool may cost significantly less, but it might not be worth the hassle of managing a separate tool and manually updating the page every time you publish a new post. On the other hand, tools like SproutLink effortlessly fit into your publishing workflow and existing social media management ecosystem.


It’s a feature you get along with tools for content planning, publishing and scheduling, making it worth the higher price point.


## Make every click count with the right link-in-bio tool


A link-in-bio tool makes all the difference between[engagements](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/social-media-engagement/) that end on social media and clicks that ultimately turn into conversions. Whether you’re looking to drive customers to your product page or get direct bookings to a consultation session, these tools streamline the journey.


And if your biggest concern is managing post links right within your usual publishing workflow, SproutLink is the best link-in-bio tool for you.[Sign up for a free 30-day trial](https://sproutsocial.com/essentials-trial/) of Sprout Essentials to see how it works.
